title: Gen-BW
fill_note: DENSE layered wind with a jig; scorer cap 0.65
fill_how: The scored turns assume a dense, layer-by-layer wind at fill 0.65 (insulated-wire area / window; the scorer cap). Use a winding jig on a drill/lathe with a turn counter, lay each layer side-by-side with light back-tension, and do not scramble-wind: a scramble wind only reaches ≈0.55–0.60 and then the window holds fewer turns (scorer what-if `--fill 0.60` is in the table above). Never wind more than the listed turns — the copper must stay below the flanges.
steel_extra: **Steel:** Ø134 × 6.35 mm (1/4") — thicker than the other kits because each 10 mm stacked pole pushes more flux into the disc (see thickness check). Same Ø134 outline and M3 map (R30 at 0/90/180/270°, R63 at 45/135/225/315°) as Gen-BO/BR, so a 1/4" cut of that DXF works.
o5_note: scan t1 showed diametric Ø5 between 90°-spaced poles LOWER the score (e.g. 1.355 vs 1.421 W in the best t1 pair), so all 48 Ø5 are spare
card_sub: all 16 Ø20 as 8 × 10 mm stacks · poles R52 · 6 bobbins r26–74 × 21.3 build × 6.75 mm copper · no O5 · Ø134 × 1/4" steel · 2026-10-10
idea: Stacked poles: two Ø20×5 per pocket (10 mm poles), 4 per rotor at R52, trading pole count for field — peak Bz at the copper rises to ≈0.73 T (vs 0.54 T on Gen-BR), which lets a thin 6.75 mm copper layer with a very deep 21 mm build carry the turns. But the electrical frequency halves, and the scorer puts it at about 45 % of Gen-BR: the thicker magnets do not make up for half the poles.
halb_block:
halbach_magnetisation = "none";  // NO O5 assist magnets in this kit (scan: they lower the 4-pole score)
rotor_b_same_axis   = true;     // same-index magnets share one axis: N faces S across the gap
